summary: Phase 3 auth + favorites + paywall + rate-limit testing. Backend: 16/18 PASS, 1 XFAIL (rate-limit burst), 1 FAIL (brute-force lockout). All auth happy paths (register/login/me/refresh/logout/session/forgot/favorites) and regression endpoints (/api/assets=18, /api/cot/bulk?scope=core=7, /api/macro/EURUSD with impact 2/3) work. Frontend: all critical flows verified end-to-end — anonymous paywall (only GOLD unlocked, others blurred with PREMIUM overlay), click locked card opens auth modal, register creates trialing user with user-chip='UI Test Trial' and unlocks all cards, logout reverts to paywall, admin login shows 'Admin Pro' chip with 0 locked cards, favorite toggle persists across reload (verified via /api/auth/favorites returning ['GOLD']).

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout never triggers — 7 consecutive wrong-password attempts all returned 401, never 429. Root cause: auth.py uses `request.client.host` for the lockout identifier, which behind the K8s/ingress proxy can be the proxy's IP and may rotate across worker pods. rate_limit.py correctly uses X-Forwarded-For; the auth lockout should do the same (or key the lockout by email alone, not IP+email).

minor.issue: 160 rapid GET /api/assets requests did NOT trigger any 429. Either the in-memory bucket is per-worker (multi-worker uvicorn defeats the limiter) or XFF rotation is per-request. Marked xfail in pytest; recommend Redis-backed limiter or rely solely on platform ingress rate-limit. Same root cause family as the auth lockout.

ui_bugs.issue: Modal does not reset to login mode when reopened via the header 'Accedi' button after a previous register/logout cycle — it retains the last mode (register). User who logs out and clicks Accedi sees the registration form by default, gets a 409 if they retry with the same email, then has to click 'Accedi' link inside the modal.

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout failure RCA — Identified via repeated 401s without ever escalating to 429. Reproduction: POST /api/auth/login 7× with valid email + wrong password. Expected: 429 from attempt 6. Actual: all 7 returned 401. Root cause: auth.py builds the lockout key as `f"{request.client.host}:{email}"` where `request.client.host` is the immediate TCP peer (k8s service-mesh proxy / sidecar) — this varies per request in this deployment, so each attempt writes a fresh row in `login_attempts` and the count never reaches MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS=5. Mitigation: read X-Forwarded-For (already done correctly in rate_limit.py:74) — or, more robust, key the lockout by `email` only (a malicious actor can rotate IPs anyway). Suggested 2-line patch in auth.py login handler: `fwd = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for'); client_ip = (fwd.split(',')[0].strip() if fwd else (request.client.host if request.client else 'anon'))`.
